subject: maths
topic: Differentiation and its applications (gradient, maxima/minima, rates)

kept.q: Find the gradient of the curve y = 5x^2 - 3x + 2 at the point where x = 1.
kept.explanation: Differentiate y = 5x^2 - 3x + 2 to get dy/dx = 10x - 3. Substitute x = 1: dy/dx = 10(1) - 3 = 7. So the gradient at x = 1 is 7.
kept.pidgin: Differentiate y = 5x^2 - 3x + 2, e go give dy/dx = 10x - 3. Put x = 1 inside: 10(1) - 3 = 7. So gradient na 7.

kept.q: A spherical balloon is being inflated so that its radius increases at a constant rate of 3 cm/s. Find the rate at which the volume is increasing when the radius is 5 cm. (Volume of sphere, V = 4/3 pi r^3)
kept.explanation: V = 4/3 pi r^3, so dV/dr = 4 pi r^2. By chain rule, dV/dt = 4 pi r^2 (dr/dt). At r = 5, dr/dt = 3: dV/dt = 4 pi (25)(3) = 300 pi cm^3/s.
kept.pidgin: V = 4/3 pi r^3, so dV/dr = 4 pi r^2. Use chain rule: dV/dt = 4 pi r^2 multiply dr/dt. For r = 5, dr/dt = 3: dV/dt = 4 pi (25)(3) = 300 pi cm^3/s.

kept.q: The curve y = x^3 - 3x^2 + 2 has gradient 9 at two distinct points. Find the sum of the x-coordinates of these two points.
kept.explanation: dy/dx = 3x^2 - 6x. Set this equal to 9: 3x^2 - 6x - 9 = 0, which simplifies to x^2 - 2x - 3 = 0, giving (x-3)(x+1) = 0, so x = 3 or x = -1. The sum of these roots is 3 + (-1) = 2.
kept.pidgin: dy/dx = 3x^2 - 6x. Make am equal to 9: 3x^2 - 6x - 9 = 0, e simplify to x^2 - 2x - 3 = 0, wey factor to (x-3)(x+1) = 0, so x = 3 or x = -1. Add dem together: 3 + (-1) = 2.

q.q: Find the maximum value of the function f(x) = x^3 - 3x^2 - 9x + 5.
q.explanation: f'(x) = 3x^2 - 6x - 9 = 0 gives x = 3 or x = -1. f''(x) = 6x - 6; at x = -1, f'' = -12 (negative), so x = -1 is a maximum point. f(-1) = -1 - 3 + 9 + 5 = 10.
